promotionalText: Prompt from the couch. Watch the turn land on your Lock Screen — thinking, tool runs, approvals — over your own tailnet. No relay, no account, no tracking.
description:
Send a prompt to Claude Code, opencode or Oh My Pi from your phone, pocket it, and watch the turn finish on your Lock Screen. Approve the risky command, answer the agent's question, read every diff — from anywhere on your own Tailscale network.

WHAT YOU NEED
A Mac or Linux machine on your tailnet (Tailscale is free for personal use) running one of your agents: opencode, Claude Code through the open-source claude-bridge, or Oh My Pi through the open-source omp-bridge. Set-up is three verified steps, and a built-in demo lets you try every screen before you wire anything.

THE TURN, LIVE ON YOUR LOCK SCREEN
• A Live Activity per conversation: what it is doing, for how long, and how many tools it has run.
• An approval request alerts you; a finished turn lingers with its outcome. Tap to land in the exact chat.
• Updates arrive by push while the app is suspended.

A NATIVE TRANSCRIPT, NOT A TERMINAL
• Streaming text written at the model's own speed, with thinking and tool runs folded into readable groups.
• Diffs, commands and their real output inline; syntax-highlighted code with byte-exact copy.
• Allow once, always, or deny — without leaving the chat. Agent questions become tappable cards.
• Queue the next message while a turn runs, edit it before it goes, or stop the turn on the server.
• Every picture the agent hands you, in a gallery you can zoom, save or share.

EVERY MACHINE ON ONE BOARD
• All your servers' conversations in one list, live status first, grouped by project.
• Read the repository before you trust the change: branch, staged, changed, untracked, and the diff of any file.
• Subagents dock inside the turn that spawned them; a compaction is drawn as a seam with what it kept.
• Slash commands from the server's own catalog, per-message model and reasoning effort, forking.

KNOW WHAT IT COSTS
• Every conversation priced, every month totalled across machines — by model, project and tool.
• Plan limits and quotas for Claude, Grok, Ollama Cloud, DeepSeek and more, on Home and in a widget.

YOURS, END TO END
• Point-to-point over your tailnet. No relay servers, no account, no analytics, nobody reading your code.
• Programmatic UIKit, Swift 6, Liquid Glass on iOS 26. Dark mode, Dynamic Type, haptics.
• Open source under GPL-3.0 — the app, the engine, and both bridges.

FREE, WITH AN HONEST PRO
The free app is the complete core: one server, full chat, approvals, attachments, models, forking, and Live Activities. Tailscode Pro is a one-time purchase, no subscription: multiple saved servers, concurrent Live Activities, and a supporter badge.

Tailscode is independent open-source software: not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic, Tailscale Inc., the opencode project or Oh My Pi.

Privacy policy: https://midgarcorp.cc/tailscode/privacy
Source code: https://github.com/guitaripod/Tailscode
reviewNotes:
Tailscode is a native client for coding-agent servers (opencode, Claude Code via the open-source claude-bridge, and Oh My Pi via the open-source omp-bridge) that developers run on their own machines and reach over their private Tailscale VPN (WireGuard). There is no account, no sign-in, and no server operated by us.

HOW TO REVIEW: the first screen offers "Try the demo" as its second button, under "Set up my machine". The demo installs two sample servers with realistic scripted sessions and exercises every feature: streaming transcripts, tool activity, inline permission approvals (open "Dark mode for the settings screen"), agent questions (open "Ship the pricing page A/B test"), the model picker, usage gauges, and the file browser (compose button). Typing in any demo chat streams a scripted reply. A DEMO badge in the navigation bar marks the sample data and leaves the demo again. No server, account, or extra hardware is needed to evaluate the app.

ATS / arbitrary loads: the app talks HTTP to hosts on the user's own WireGuard-encrypted tailnet (CGNAT 100.64/10 addresses); such hosts cannot present CA-signed certificates for raw IPs, and traffic never crosses the public internet in plaintext.

In-app purchases: Tailscode Pro is a one-time convenience unlock (multiple saved servers, concurrent Live Activities, supporter badge); the three tips are voluntary. The complete core is free, and nothing is disabled if an entitlement lapses.
whatsNew:
Clearing out a week of dead chats no longer takes a week of taps.

Select several conversations at once and delete, archive, save or mark them read in one gesture. Every verb counts what it would touch before you commit to it, a delete names what goes and cannot be undone quietly, and if the server only manages some of them Tailscode says which.

Starting a chat is one screen now. Instead of a file browser pushed full-screen, the New Conversation sheet ranks the folders this phone already knows for that server — the ones you starred, the ones you used recently, and the ones your own chats are working in — against whatever you type, showing how many chats live in each. Type a path it has never seen and it is offered as its own row. The server you used last is already chosen. With a hardware keyboard attached the whole sheet is drivable without touching the screen.

The chat list is grouped again: Pinned, Live Now, Saved, Recent. A conversation is Live the moment this phone can see the turn running rather than whenever the server's next sweep agrees, one that stopped to ask you something says Needs You, and a chat you are watching is never painted offline because its server missed a single listing.

Transcripts got shorter. A run of agent steps collapses to a slim line and only grows into the full card when you open it — there is a switch in Settings if you prefer the roomier shape. Turns now open with air around them, so a long conversation reads as turns rather than one column.

Long-press the app icon for New Chat, Saved Chats, Usage, Quick Ask, or Resume — which goes straight back to the conversation you were last in.

Chats no longer get lost between projects: the session list shows every conversation on a server, from whichever folder it started in.
